title: Can the Note Be Written?

concept.title: Count what is available, spend what is needed
body: To cut a note out of a magazine you need, for every letter, **at least as many copies** in the magazine as the note contains. Count the letters of the magazine in a map. Then go through the note and spend one copy for every letter: if the count is not positive, the note cannot be written.
This "inventory" pattern (count the supply, subtract the demand) is useful in many problems: anagrams, building a word from tiles, checking that one multiset contains another.

statement: You want to cut the letters of a note out of a magazine. Each letter of the magazine can be used once. Print `yes` if the note can be made from the magazine, otherwise print `no`.
inputFormat: The first line has the note.
The second line has the magazine.
constraints: 1 <= length of the note, length of the magazine <= 20000

examples.note: The magazine has two a and one b.

hints: Count the letters of the magazine.
For each letter of the note, take one copy away.
If a letter is not available, the answer is no.

note = input().strip()
